summary: Rate-fencing and "credit bleed" seen as soft 429s during simultaneous heartbeat probes and multipart batch import
description:
Issue summary: Customer reports a recurring wave of soft 429 responses during a large multipart embedding import that runs concurrently with frequent heartbeat probes from their orchestrator. Impact: ~15% of batch upload attempts see transient 429s causing retries and backoff loops; customer sees increased tail latency and several job failures. Environment: Dedicated pool, region: us-east primary with failover to eu-west; orchestrator issues signed URL uploads and emits ~1s heartbeat probes per pod.

Observed behavior: During import windows (10k+ small files over 15 minutes) we see periodic drops in available burst credits attributed to heartbeat and healthcheck probes counted against the same refill window as the batch, resulting in temporary token depletion and 429s. Customer expects healthchecks to be excluded or accounted against a separate background pool.

Expected behavior: Heartbeat/healthcheck traffic should not exhaust burst credits used by customer-initiated multipart uploads (or should be configurable to separate pools).

Urgency: Customer-facing ingestion jobs are failing intermittently; they are on Dedicated plan and have a requirement for predictable bulk ingest throughput.
steps_to_reproduce:
1) Provision a dedicated tenant in us-east with a burstable quota and a background healthcheck frequency of 1s per worker.
2) Start an orchestrator that requests signed URLs and uploads 10k files via multipart sessions over 10-20 minutes using 50 parallel workers.
3) Simultaneously enable per-pod heartbeat probes (1s cadence) that call an edge health endpoint.
4) Observe the rate-limiter metrics and client responses during the peak window.
5) Expected: sustained throughput with minimal 429s; Actual: saw clustered 429 waves aligned with refill window boundaries and ingress probe bursts.

[2026-03-10T14:03:11Z] proxy.rate_counter[tenant=atlasmaps] refill_window=60s credits_before=250 credits_after=0 reason=heartbeat_probe_counts
[2026-03-10T14:03:12Z] upstream.response tenant=atlasmaps code=429 route=/v1/upload multipart_id=abc123 worker=10
[2026-03-10T14:03:12Z] client.retry scheduled backoff=250ms attempt=1
[2026-03-10T14:03:13Z] proxy.metrics token_leak_detected window=60s delta=-245 source=edge-healthcheck]
investigation_notes:
Initial hypothesis: edge healthchecks are counted against tenant burst credits because they hit the same edge route and are not excluded by route weight or priority.
What we checked: token refill timing (60s window), aggregated heartbeat traffic from customer's pod fleet, signed URL callback paths normalization, and edge proxy path rules.
Findings: 1) Heartbeat path uses /health/tenant/lookup which matches a catch-all ingress route that inherits tenant token accounting. 2) Refill window aligned with peak probe cadence leading to sawtooth depletion patterns. 3) Dedicated pool had no separate background/burst pool configured for long-lived SSE or probe traffic. 4) No rate-limiter bug found in core refill algorithm; behavior is by policy accounting and route-match inheritance.
Open action items: (a) Provide immediate customer mitigation steps to isolate healthchecks, (b) propose a configuration change to split background probes into an exempt pool or lower-cost background lane, (c) draft a short-term console guidance update for dedicated tenants, (d) consider a product follow-up to add an explicit 'probe exemption' rule for edge health endpoints.
comments: 2026-03-10 - Aisha Khan (Support): Customer submitted logs and example orchestrator config. Noted high heartbeat freq (1s) from 120 pods. Assigned to Tom R.

2026-03-10 - Tom Reynolds (SRE): Confirmed refill window alignment. Reproduced locally with a scaled-down harness; probe calls counted under tenant route. Temporarily recommended reducing heartbeat cadence to 10s as mitigation.

2026-03-11 - Mei Chen (Platform Eng): Suggested creating a split-route rule that maps /health/* to a background lane with separate quota. Filed INT-902500 as an engineering task for a short-term routing rule template.

2026-03-11 - Customer (AtlasMaps SRE): Applied heartbeat cadence change; reported decrease in 429s but still saw periodic soft-throttle during large parallel uploads. Asked for guidance to permanently segregate probe traffic in Dedicated.

2026-03-12 - Tom Reynolds (SRE): Implemented a temporary ingress rule to route health check requests to a low-cost background pool for this tenant (edge config change). Monitoring shows burst credits stable for 3 hours.
2026-03-12 - Support: Noted next steps: coordinate with Product to add UI guidance + include runbook for Dedicated customers. Customer to validate overnight bulk imports and report status.
resolution: Workaround applied: Temporary ingress rule routing /health/* to a background quota lane for the tenant; recommended customer reduce heartbeat to >=10s and re-run bulk import. Long-term: product team to add a 'probe exemption' template for Dedicated customers and a console option to configure separate background pools. Ticket remains open until product change is scheduled and customer validates overnight run (monitoring window).
